A.depoimento: My armies have marched to claim the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora. With spearmen leading at Santarem and archers at Evora, I expect to secure both. I have left my knights at the capital and am building more troops to sustain my campaign across the peninsula.
A.plano: I am sending all spearmen to Santarem and all archers to Evora to capture both villages. I keep my knights at the capital for defense and build two more spearmen. Next turn I will explore from my new villages and continue expanding. I must be cautious and aim to hold 18 villages for two turns.

B.depoimento: I march all my troops to take Tarragona, while my smiths forge two new spearman. The expansion has begun!
B.plano: Capture Tarragona (21) with my full army now, then Girona (23) next turn. Build spearman continuously to grow my forces. After securing the coast, push inland toward Zaragoza (17) and Madrid (12) to claim neutral villages and expand my territory. Need to reach 18 villages to win.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a coordinated strike. Tarragona's troops are splitting to capture Castellon and Zaragoza, exploiting the counter triangle to minimize losses. Barcelona is building spearman for the assault on Girona, and my knights remain at Tarragona as a rapid reaction force. This expansion will bring me to five villages by next turn.
B.plano: This turn, build 2 spearman at Barcelona and keep the garrison there. Split Tarragona's army: send a small archer-led force to Castellon (using the counter bonus) and a spearman-led force to Zaragoza (also with counter). Leave the 3 knights at Tarragona as a reserve. Next turn, use Barcelona's reinforced 4 spearman to take Girona, while the newly captured Castellon and Zaragoza launch attacks into Valencia, Teruel, and Madrid. Continue building troops to reach 18 villages.

A.depoimento: My armies march on Coimbra to claim it for the crown. My craftsmen forge new weapons to strengthen our ranks. Reinforcements rush to support our vanguard. The kingdom expands!
A.plano: We are attacking Coimbra with Santarem's spearmen to expand. We are building knights in Lisboa and spearmen in Santarem and Evora to strengthen our forces. We are sending reinforcements from Lisboa to Santarem. Next turn, we will assess the battle and decide whether to push north or attack Badajoz. We must explore from Coimbra. We decided not to attack Faro yet to build up a mixed army with spearmen.

B.depoimento: Turn 3: Our forces have successfully consolidated our holdings of Castellon and Zaragoza. This turn, we launch a dual offensive: Barcelona's spearman march on Girona, while Zaragoza's spear-led army strikes Huesca, exploiting our counter advantage against their knights. Tarragona's knights are redeployed to Castellon to prepare for the assault on Valencia next turn. We are building 2 spearman at both Barcelona and Tarragona to sustain our expansion.
B.plano: We will expand on two fronts this turn. On the east, Barcelona's 4 spearman will take Girona [23]. On the west, Zaragoza's 3 spearman and 2 archers will take Huesca [20] using the spearman-vs-knight counter. Tarragona's 3 knights will march to Castellon [18] to reinforce it for next turn's push on Valencia [16]. We will build 2 spearman at Barcelona and 2 spearman at Tarragona to replenish our ranks. Next turn, we will attack Valencia from Castellon and continue building our army to reach 18 villages.

A.depoimento: We have consolidated our hold on Coimbra and now we strike at the neutral villages of Badajoz and Faro to expand our territory. Our knights and spearmen march from Santarem and Evora, while Lisboa sends its knights to reinforce Santarem for the next phase of our campaign.
A.plano: Attack Badajoz from Santarem and Faro from Evora to expand our territory. Build knights in Santarem and Evora, and spearmen in Lisboa. Send reinforcements from Lisboa to Santarem. Next turn, we will assess the battles and plan the next expansion towards Porto and Salamanca from Coimbra.

B.depoimento: Our armies have taken Girona and Huesca. Now we strike at Valencia and Pamplona to expand our realm. Castellon's knights lead the assault on Valencia, while Huesca's spearmen and archers attack Pamplona. We are building new troops to sustain our momentum.
B.plano: This turn we attack Valencia [16] from Castellon [18] and Pamplona [19] from Huesca [20] to expand our territory. We reinforce Zaragoza [17] from Tarragona [21], Huesca [20] from Girona [23], and Tarragona [21] from Barcelona [22]. We build knights at Barcelona and Tarragona, and spearman at Castellon and Zaragoza to replenish our forces. Next turn we will push west towards Madrid [12] and Teruel [13] to secure our borders and continue our expansion towards the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn, we focused on rapid expansion and reinforcement. We built new knights in Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora, and an archer in Coimbra. We marched 3 knights from Santarem to Coimbra to prepare for the assault on Porto, while moving troops from Lisboa to Santarem. From Badajoz, we launched a double offensive, sending 2 knights to Toledo and a mixed force to Sevilha to secure new territories.
A.plano: Expand aggressively from Badajoz by sending 2 knights to Toledo and 4 spearman + 1 knight to Sevilha. Reinforce Coimbra with 3 knights from Santarem, and move troops from Lisboa to Santarem. Build knights in Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, and an archer in Coimbra to grow our army. Next turn, we will assess the battles at Toledo and Sevilha, and prepare to attack Porto from Coimbra once reinforced.

B.depoimento: This turn we ordered the assault on Teruel with our elite knights, while our forces in Huesca made the ultimate sacrifice to weaken Pamplona's knight garrison. We are building up our knight corps across our core villages to strike at Madrid next. The path to the enemy capital is opening up.
B.plano: We attack Teruel [13] with Valencia's knights and archers, and sacrifice the Huesca army to clear Pamplona [19], followed by spearmen from Huesca and Zaragoza to take it. We build knights at Barcelona, Tarragona, Castellon, and Zaragoza, and spearmen at Girona and Huesca. Next turn we will have 9 villages and will push towards Madrid [12] with our gathered knights, then expand west towards the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn, we focus on expanding our empire by targeting the neutral villages of Porto and Sevilha. We send our elite knights to assault Porto, while our army from Badajoz is poised to take Sevilha. To protect our newly gained border at Toledo, we march troops from Santarem, supported by reinforcements from our capital Lisboa. We also send Faro's archers to support the Sevilha campaign. Our workshops are busy producing knights and archers to sustain our military might.
A.plano: Conquer Porto with 3 knights from Coimbra and Sevilha with the marching army. Reinforce Toledo from Santarem and Santarem from Lisboa to secure our western border. Send Faro's troops to Sevilha for reinforcement. Build knights and archers to grow our army. Next turn, assess the battles and prepare to attack Cordoba or Salamanca.

B.depoimento: Victory is within our grasp! The spearmen have cleared Pamplona, and now our knights strike Madrid and Toledo simultaneously. We are building at full capacity, replacing our marching troops and preparing for the push into the enemy heartland. The net of villages is closing around King A's territory!
B.plano: We have conquered Teruel and are about to conquer Pamplona with the marching spearmen. This turn, we launch a double strike: Zaragoza's knights take Madrid, and Teruel's knights take Toledo. We also send spearmen to reinforce Pamplona and the northern route, and move coastal knights towards Zaragoza to build up the central strike force. We build knights and spearmen across our villages to replace losses and grow our army. Next turn, we will have 11 villages and will push west from Madrid and Toledo towards Salamanca and Badajoz, aiming to encircle the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launched a coordinated strike: Porto's knights marched on Salamanca while our Santarem army advanced on Toledo. We heavily reinforced Badajoz with troops from Lisboa, Santarem, Coimbra, and Evora to fortify our border. We began concentrating archers in Sevilha for the upcoming assault on Cordoba, and started moving spearmen towards Porto to prepare for the attack on Vigo. Our building orders focused on producing the specific troop types we need: knights for the northern front, archers for the south, and spearmen for the west.
A.plano: We are attacking Salamanca with Porto's knights and Toledo with Santarem's army. We are reinforcing Badajoz with troops from Santarem, Lisboa, Coimbra, and Evora to secure our border. We are sending archers from Faro and Evora to Sevilha to gather forces for Cordoba. We have started moving spearmen from Coimbra to Porto for the Vigo campaign. Our builds produce knights, archers, and spearmen to support these operations. Next turn, we will evaluate the battles and plan the next attacks on Madrid and Cordoba.

B.depoimento: The enemy marched on Toledo, so we gathered every fast troop we could and sent them to reinforce the defense. Our villages worked to build new spearmen and knights to replenish our forces. The defense of Toledo is now strong, and we await the enemy's assault.
B.plano: Our immediate priority is to hold Toledo against the incoming enemy army. We have rushed all available fast troops from Castellon, Zaragoza, Teruel, and Madrid to reinforce the garrison. Our villages are building spearmen and knights to rebuild our forces. Once the enemy assault is repelled, we will launch a counteroffensive from Toledo against Badajoz, and from Madrid against Burgos, aiming to expand our territory and reach the 18-victory threshold.

A.depoimento: Our armies advanced on multiple fronts today. The knight from Salamanca marched to claim the empty city of Madrid, while Sevilha's archers and knight assaulted Cordoba. We flooded Badajoz with reinforcements from across our realm to deter the enemy's heavy forces in Toledo. New troops were built to sustain our campaigns.
A.plano: Attack Madrid with Salamanca's knight; take Cordoba with Sevilha's archers and knight. Flood Badajoz with reinforcements from Santarem, Faro, Evora, Sevilha, Lisboa. Send follow-up from Badajoz to Madrid and Cordoba. Next turn: assess battles, reinforce Salamanca, plan Vigo and northern exploration. Remember to build troops.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launched a decisive blow against the enemy's stronghold at Badajoz, sending our elite knights and archers from Toledo to crush their garrison. At the same time, we rushed spearman and knights from our interior villages to reinforce Madrid and Toledo, securing our borders against any counterattack. Our armies are on the move, and our villages are working tirelessly to build the forces needed for total victory.
B.plano: Our campaign focuses on eliminating the enemy's strongest forces and expanding our territory. This turn, we strike at Badajoz with our knights and archers from Toledo, aiming to destroy the enemy's main army and capture the village. We simultaneously reinforce Madrid with spearman and knights from Zaragoza, Huesca, Pamplona, and Valencia to secure our capital's approaches. In the coming turns, we will build on our momentum, attacking Salamanca from Madrid and the neutral villages of Burgos and Cordoba to reach the 18-victory threshold. Our interior villages continue producing troops to feed th

A.depoimento: I have launched a massive multi-village assault on Badajoz, sending 18 troops from five of my villages to overwhelm the enemy garrison. Simultaneously, I have opened two new fronts: sending Porto's army to attack the neutral Vigo, and Cordoba's troops to attack Murcia, aiming to bypass the heavily fortified Madrid and Toledo and reach the enemy's northern territories.
A.plano: Conquer Badajoz with the massive wave of troops from Lisboa, Santarem, Faro, Salamanca, Sevilha. Next turn, march from Badajoz to Toledo and Madrid. Also, attack Vigo with Porto's troops and Murcia with Cordoba's troops to open the northern front. Remember to build troops in all villages.

B.depoimento: This turn we prepare our armies, sending reinforcements to Madrid and Toledo while fortifying Badajoz against the coming storm. Our builders work overtime, and our troops march to their staging points. We are poised to strike hard next turn.
B.plano: This turn we focus on building up our armies and reinforcing our border villages for a major offensive next turn. We build spearman and archers in all villages, sending knights and spearman to Madrid and Toledo to create powerful strike forces. We reinforce Badajoz with 2 spearman to defend against the expected enemy attack. Next turn, we will attack Salamanca from Madrid and Cordoba from Toledo with overwhelming force, aiming to capture both and bring our village count to 14. Then we will push on to Faro, Santarem, and the neutral villages to reach 18.

A.depoimento: Turn 10: I built troops in every village and set up two offensives. Porto will take the neutral Vigo next turn with three knights, giving me a northern base and extra income. At Santarem I'm gathering spearsmen for a proper assault on Badajoz, while reinforcing Salamanca with a knight and archers against Madrid. The two small waves already marching to Badajoz will fail again - I'm done wasting troops there until I have a real striking force.
A.plano: PLAN: Capture Vigo next turn (3 knights from Porto, attack 12 > 10). Gather spearman at Santarem for Badajoz (~turn 13): receive from Lisboa/Coimbra, keep building. Salamanca reinforced (knight + 2 archer); if Madrid attacks it may fall - accept and counter later. Do NOT attack Badajoz until Santarem has 8+ spearman with support. Build in all villages every turn.

B.depoimento: In a bold triple strike, we captured Cordoba, Salamanca, and Murcia, while reinforcing Badajoz against enemy attacks. Our armies overwhelmed the defenses, and we are now at 15 villages. The interior is building and sending reinforcements to the front. We are poised to expand further next turn.
B.plano: Triple offensive: take Cordoba (Toledo), Salamanca (Madrid), Murcia (Valencia). Reinforce Badajoz with knight from Toledo. Send all interior troops to Madrid/Toledo to maintain garrisons. Build in all villages. This brings us to 15 villages. Next turn: push from Cordoba to Sevilha/Faro, from Salamanca to Coimbra/Porto, explore unexplored. Goal: 18 villages or eliminate enemy.

A.depoimento: I am strengthening my borders and preparing for the assault on Vigo. My troops are building, and reinforcements are on the way. The enemy may attack, but I am ready.
A.plano: I am building in all villages to increase my forces. I sent spearman from Lisbon to Santarem and from Evora to Faro to reinforce my borders. I will attack Vigo next turn with Porto's knights and newly built spearman. I need to watch for enemy attacks on Coimbra and Porto, and continue gathering spearman at Santarem for the eventual attack on Badajoz.

B.depoimento: King B launches a coordinated offensive! Cordoba's full strength strikes at Sevilha, while Toledo and Valencia rush to reinforce the line. Badajoz sends a supporting force. In the north, we mass troops in Salamanca for the next push. All villages work to build more spearmen. The enemy will not hold!
B.plano: Focus on southern front: attack Sevilha from Cordoba with 11 spearmen. Send reinforcements from Toledo, Valencia, and Badajoz to support the assault and hold captured territory. In the north, transfer troops from Madrid to Salamanca to build up for an attack on Coimbra/Porto next turn. Build spearmen in all villages to replenish and grow our army. Aim to capture Sevilha, then Faro, then northern villages to reach 18 villages.

A.depoimento: This turn, I strengthened Sevilha's defenses with a massive reinforcement from Faro, hoping to repel the enemy's double attack. I launched an attack on Vigo with a clever mix of spearman and knights to exploit the counter triangle. I also reinforced my other borders and built up my armies across my kingdom.
A.plano: I am reinforcing Sevilha with a large force from Faro to defend against the two enemy armies. I am attacking Vigo with a mixed force from Porto to gain a village, using a tie in troop counts to get the counter bonus. I am sending reinforcements from Lisbon to Santarem, Santarem to Coimbra, Coimbra to Porto, and Evora to Faro to maintain strong borders. I am building troops in all villages to increase my forces.

B.depoimento: King B's forces launch a triple offensive! In the north, Salamanca's elite march on Porto while Madrid strikes at Burgos. In the south, Cordoba's troops join the assault on Sevilha, hoping to crush the enemy after the initial waves from Murcia and Badajoz weaken the garrison. We build spearmen across the realm to fuel the endless war. The path to 18 villages is clear!
B.plano: Focus on three fronts this turn: attack Porto from Salamanca, Burgos from Madrid, and Sevilha from Cordoba to finish the southern push. Send reinforcements from Toledo to Cordoba and Zaragoza to Madrid to maintain momentum. Build spearmen in all villages to grow our army. Aim to capture Porto, Burgos, and Sevilha next turn to reach 18 villages and secure the win condition.

A.depoimento: My forces have conquered Sevilha, expanding my territory to 7 villages. I am building knights across the realm to prepare for the next major push. Reinforcements are moving to secure the new southern border and strengthen Santarem for the upcoming assault on Badajoz.
A.plano: Building knights in all villages to boost army. Sending Lisboa's knight to Santarem to prepare for attack on Badajoz. Sending Evora's spearman to Faro, and Faro's troops to Sevilha to reinforce after conquest. Focus on south expansion via Sevilha to Cordoba. Do not attack Porto or Salamanca yet, too strong. Keep Vigo defended.

B.depoimento: We have reached the victory threshold of 18 villages! Now we must hold the line. The enemy is attacking Sevilha, so we are rushing all available spearman from Cordoba to reinforce it and repel the assault. We keep our other borders strong and build spearman across the empire to ensure we have the manpower to defend our hard-won territory.
B.plano: We have reached the victory threshold of 18 villages. This turn is purely defensive to secure the win condition of holding 18 villages for 2 consecutive turns. The enemy is attacking Sevilha, so we send all 8 spearman from Cordoba to reinforce it. We do not weaken other border villages like Badajoz to keep our defenses strong. We build spearman in all possible villages to grow our army for future operations.

A.depoimento:
This turn we focused on building archers, as knights are countered by spearmen.
We reinforced our border villages to deter enemy attacks.
The Sevilha force will be lost, but we are readying a strong attack on Badajoz.
A.plano:
Building archers everywhere to counter enemy spearmen.
Reinforcing Santarem with Coimbra's archer and Lisboa's knight.
Reinforcing Faro with Evora's knight.
Preparing attack on Badajoz from Santarem next turn.

B.depoimento: The enemy is attacking Sevilha, so we rush reinforcements from Cordoba and Badajoz to defend our southern stronghold. We build spearman across all our villages to grow our army and secure our borders.
B.plano: The enemy is attacking Sevilha this turn. We reinforce it with all available troops from Cordoba and Badajoz to ensure it holds. We build 2 spearman in every village to maximize our troop production and prepare for future offensives. Once Sevilha is secure, we will look to push into enemy territory from the southern front.
